recent_posts.Post Message: Last night was one to remember. 🏅🌟 At the 2026 Sabin Awards Ceremony, we celebrated immunization trailblazers who have left an indelible mark on public health.   Professor Özlem Türeci accepted the Albert B. Sabin Gold Medal on behalf of herself and her partner, Professor Uğur Şahin, for their role in turning the tide of the COVID-19 pandemic and their efforts to support access to novel medicines globally.   Dr. Senjuti Saha was named the 2026 Sabin Rising Star for using genomics to inform the rollout of the world’s largest typhoid vaccine program, protecting millions of children in Bangladesh.  Read more about their accomplishments, and watch the livestream of the ceremony ⤵️ https://ow.ly/zqM250YZ6fC  BioNTech SE | Child Health Research Foundation (CHRF)

This month, Sabin President of Research & Development Kelly Warfield and CEO Amy Finan traveled to Addis Ababa to meet with officials from the Ethiopia Ministry of Health, Armauer Hansen Research Institute, Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations - CEPI, IQVIA, U.S. CDC, and other partners.  The conversations focused on lessons learned from the 2025 Marburg outbreak response, which included Sabin’s cAd3-Marburg Vaccine in a Phase 2 clinical trial. From supply chains and infrastructure to community engagement, data management and health workforce training, the visit offered valuable insights into what it takes to move quickly, collaboratively, and effectively during an outbreak response.

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing health threat worldwide. 🦠  AMR happens when bacteria and viruses encounter antibiotics and become resistant to them, no longer responding to the medicines designed to kill them. Infections become harder to treat, increasing the risk of disease spread, severe illness, and death.  #VaccinesWork to prevent AMR by preventing disease and therefore preventing antibiotic use, lowering the chances for resistant bacteria to develop and spread.   Swipe ➡️ for what you need to know.

top_post.post_message: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing health threat worldwide. 🦠  AMR happens when bacteria and viruses encounter antibiotics and evolve to develop a resistance to them, thus no longer responding to the medicines designed to kill them. Infections become harder to treat, increasing the risk of disease spread, severe illness, and death.  #VaccinesWork to prevent AMR by preventing disease and therefore preventing antibiotic use, lowering the chances for resistant bacteria to develop and spread.   Learn more ⤵️ https://ow.ly/FLK250YUK39

This month, Sabin President of Research & Development Kelly Lyn Warfield and CEO Amy Finan traveled to Addis Ababa to meet with officials from the Ethiopia Ministry of Health, Armauer Hansen Research Institute, CEPI (Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations), IQVIA, U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and other partners.  The conversations focused on lessons learned from the 2025 Marburg outbreak response, which included Sabin’s cAd3-Marburg Vaccine in a Phase 2 clinical trial. From supply chains and infrastructure to community engagement, data management and health workforce training, the visit offered valuable insights into what it takes to move quickly, collaboratively, and effectively during an outbreak response.

board.public_perception_text: Sabin's social media presence continues to strengthen institutional reputation. Our messaging reaches diverse stakeholder groups with strong engagement metrics. Positive sentiment reflects public confidence in our vaccine research and immunization initiatives.
board.donor_engagement_text: Social channels serve as critical touchpoints for demonstrating research impact and organizational effectiveness. Quarterly reports of breakthrough achievements drive stakeholder engagement and support fundraising objectives. Expanding reach indicates growing influence in vaccine policy discussions.
board.risk_management_text: Consistent engagement monitoring identifies potential reputational risks early. Current positioning addresses vaccine concerns and establishes Sabin as trusted authority. Social media serves as early warning system enabling rapid response to misinformation.

assumptions: Reach and impressions are standardized into one visibility metric per platform, using impressions when available and otherwise reach.
Report-facing summary cards use Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn only so the dashboard and quarterly report share one scope.
Cross-network post engagements continue to come from Hootsuite's Post engagement aggregate, with X removed when legacy X totals are present.
Report-facing engagement totals stay aligned to Hootsuite's engagement definition and do not add link clicks on top.
Owly tracked-click exports are the report-facing website-resource click metric for Facebook and LinkedIn posts; X/Twitter Owly tables are optional when present.
YouTube follower counts remain available in raw Hootsuite exports, but report-facing summary cards exclude YouTube until a matching platform detail layer is maintained.
Actual follower pace uses real January 1 follower counts when they can be recovered from January exports or saved January dashboard artifacts.
Target pace remains a separate benchmark derived from the stated year-end target and annual growth rate.

Monthly export completeness is complete only when the cross-platform aggregate export, Facebook/Instagram/LinkedIn full post-performance exports, and the expected Facebook/LinkedIn Owly website-click exports are present.
Email exports are excluded from social platform calculations to avoid mixing unlike metrics.
Follower pace is labeled slightly behind when actual performance is within 5% of the benchmark pace.
